Several people were injured after an explosion occured in an Intel factory in Kiryat Gat on Wednesday, Magen David Adom confirmed.

At least three people were seriously injured, Magen David Adom said.

Israel's Fire and Rescue Authority also reported that hazardous chemicals had possibly leaked as a result of the explosion, and that they were currently working to locate the source of the chemicals, as well as extinguish the ensuing fire.

Intel’s Kiryat Gat factory manufactures semiconductor chips and is also known as FAB 28.

This is a developing story.
snapshot.title: Kiryat Gat Intel's factory sees at least three people injured in explosion - The Jerusalem Post

LONG BEACH, Calif., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB) ("Rocket Lab" or "the Company"), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today shared an update on the Neutron launch vehicle development program, including an adjusted schedule for Neutron's inaugural launch, which is now expected to occur in 2027.

A presentation discussing further details of this Neutron update is hosted on Rocket Lab's investor relations website at https://investors.rocketlabcorp.com/events-presentations/presentations

Rocket Lab Media Murielle Bakermedia@rocketlabusa.com

Investor RelationsPatrick Vorenkampinvestors@rocketlabusa.com

About Rocket LabRocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB) is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Driven by its industry-leading small-lift rockets Electron and HASTE and its upcoming reusable Neutron medium-lift rocket, Rocket Lab delivers reliable and responsive launch for the world's most important missions from constellation deployment to missile defense. Rocket Lab's satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com.
